d:
The bearer of this writ is entitled to payment in the form of an insignia of their choice upon completion of the contracted work order.
Work Order AL-473:
10 Major Mana Potions.
All filled orders should be delivered to Packmaster Stonebruiser at Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands.
Contract is null and void if tampered with or damaged.
-Dispatch Commander Metz, The Argent Dawn
c: The utility of these should go without saying.
dwarf-male

c:
Packmaster Stonebruiser pops open one of the greater arcane protection potions and take a swig.
WOOT! These pack a kick, baby! A kick I say!

Do you know what the troops on the front lines call these? Priests in a bottle...
"I'm your priest in a bott-le baby... You gotta drink me the right way..."
What's the matter sonny? It's a very popular song around these parts.
dwarf-male

d:
Zanza can create many ancient troll enchantments with proper components! Have you heard of the Savage Guard? No, of course you haven't. Your mind is addled with the inferior elven magic.
Bring me an arcanum of elven creation so that I may destroy the aberration. Do this and the Savage Guard will be yours.
troll-male
c:
The worthless magic in these enchantments fuels my anger. My anger gives me strength.
Bring me more and you shall receive another Savage Guard.
troll-male

d:
Ah, the Ice Guard. It is a thin sheen of protective magic that covers certain pieces of equipment. Those that do battle with creatures of frost and ice will gain increased protection from their attacks by using the Ice Guard.
As with all things the Wrathcaster creates, there is a price - a price that I will not lower, regardless of how much you whimper. Interested?
human-male
p: If it were not for these Argent Dawn guards, you would be a stain upon this floor.
c: Enjoy the repair costs, traveler. Naxxramas is 'unkind' to the uninitiated.
human-male

d:
A creation of genius! Much like the Ice Guard, the Shadow Guard employs a thin sheen of protective magic that covers certain pieces of equipment. And like the Ice Guard, the Shadow Guard is going to cost you a good amount of money.
Interested?
human-male
p: Be gone, insect, lest you have something for me.
c: What are you still standing around for, traveler? Our business is done.
human-male

p: Choose carefully. There are no refunds.
c: Good day, friend. It was a pleasure doing business with you.

d:
Ramaladni was a warrior of the Brotherhood - a pupil of Highlord Mograine before the Dawn even existed! When news of Mograine's death reached him, hatred and anger took over.
Understand this, friend, when rage and retribution take the reins, a man ceases to be a man. The man personifies the emotions that control him instead. And so it would be that Ramaladni, the spirit of retribution, would enter Naxxramas to exact vengeance... And never return.
Enter Naxxramas and find what became of Ramaladni.
human-male
c:
It is his ring! But it is destroyed. No other evidence of Ramaladni was found?
This does not bode well for Ramaladni. The ring, however... It might be salvageable.
human-male

d: Fixing this band may prove to be quite challenging, friend. You see, it was made from the very runes that form inside Scourge structures - like Naxxramas. Additional materials are also required but your main concern should be getting those frozen runes. Bring me what I need and I will restore the ring to its former glory.
human-male
p: Frozen runes could probably be found inside Naxxramas.
c: Ramaladni himself couldn't have done better! Here is the ring, as promised.
human-male

d:
You fancy yourself a hero of the Dawn, eh? I've seen our greatest soldiers get rolled over by Kel'Thuzad's plebes! How well could someone so clueless possibly fare in Naxxramas?
Bah, what choice do I got? You're the best I can do; I may as well help you.
Omarion left me with one recipe. It's the only song I know... I can make a few variations of these pants; you just gotta supply the materials.
dwarf-male
p: You haven't run into Omarion, have you?
c: That's some hard work! Enjoy the pants, adventurer. At least you'll die in a clean pair now.
dwarf-male

d:
Wilhelm,
If you are reading this, I have perished - finally. I want you to know that my dying thoughts revolved around you and your ineptitude when it comes to tradeskills. Unfortunately, the bearer of this handbook is in even worse shape than you in regards to crafting.
About the book: These are the rest of my recipes. Make the bearer of this book whatever they request. I'm sure you will charge a hefty fee for your services because you are, after all, a bastard.
In Disdain,
Omarion
p: Is that what I think it is?
c:
He musta really been off his rocker when he wrote this! Omarion and I - we were thick as thieves!
Anyhow, this certainly opens up some new possibilities, friend. I am now able to craft more items - for a small fee and material charges, of course.
dwarf-male

d: Thanks to you and Omarion, may he rest in peace, I am now able to create Icebane gauntlets. All you need to do is bring me the materials and pay a small crafting fee.
dwarf-male
c: Here is your order, friend. Delivered as promised!
dwarf-male

d:
Friend,
In times past you have served the interests of the Argent Dawn, always to the best of your abilities. Now, once again, we sound the clarion call in our time of greatest need.
Friend, please report to the Keeper of the Rolls at Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands if you are willing to aid us once more.
Ishnu-alah, traveler. Show me proof of the demise of a Lord of the Abyssal Council and I shall reward you with an item that should aid you in your battles against the Qiraji.
nightelf-female
p: Fandu-dath-belore? Oh, pardon me, friend. I did not recognize you. Have you the scepter?
c:
Ande'thoras-ethil. It means; 'May your troubles be diminished,' in my native tongue.
Wear the band proudly and in good health, friend.
nightelf-female

d:
With the frame formed, Atiesh is nearly whole. Only the head and base of the staff are now missing. There is also a minor issue regarding the staff being a conduit for Sargeras's evil.
Find someone that can assist you in locating the remaining pieces and exorcising the evil from the staff.
c:
The archmages have died.
Do not mourn their passing, friend. All such things are fated. Just as you holding the staff of the Guardian was fated...

d:
You question why you are still alive. After all, you have in your possession an item of great evil. The answer is not clear, friend. I only do as I must.
Kel'Thuzad sits atop his throne in Naxxramas, plotting... He seeks that which you hold and holds that which you seek.
As for the base of the staff; the dwarf, Brann Bronzebeard, held it when he entered Ahn'Qiraj. He has left Ahn'Qiraj but the base of Atiesh remains.
Should you succeed in recovering the pieces, return them to me.
p: In its current form, the staff is far too dangerous to be in the hands of a mortal.
c: There is a being within... A being not of this world.

d:
This final task will be the most difficult of all, friend. You have faced and defeated both an Old God and the Lich King's General, but now you must face the hand of Sargeras.
Take the staff to Stratholme. It is there that you will find a piece of consecrated earth: ground where the greatest knights of Lordaeron were murdered. Place the befouled staff upon the holy ground and prepare for an entity of immense power to break from within... Defeat the demonic being that controls the staff and return to me.
c: The magnitude of this accomplishment must not be understated, friend. You have done what most would have thought to be impossible. Alas, it was fated. The staff has made its choice...

p:
That mangy dog, Revilgaz, has offered to pardon any former Bloodsails willing to turn on their cap'n! That bilge sucker asked me to go an' off me ole' mates and to bring back their bandannas as proof.
I don't have it in me heart to do that, nor will I ask ye to. Bring me some silk cloth and red dye and I'll make suitable replicas. I'll tell the Baron you went turncoat, but be warned... The Bloodsails are not gonna like it!
c:
Let us observe a minute of silence for our fallen mates, friend.
Being a traitor is one thing, murdering yer own buckos... That'd be just downright despicable, aye!

d:
The Scourge is camped upon our very doorstep; we cannot remain idle! Surely you will step up to defend Stormwind from these accursed invaders?
There are strange runic circles outside, glowing with the same energy that surrounds the undead and the Necropolis above. They have significance, I'm certain, and I want you to find out what. Thin the numbers of those aberrations while you're at it; bring me proof of their death along with your results, and I will reward you. Go!
human-male
p: Have you investigated the invasion yet? There's no time for dawdling!
c: Hmm. From what you've told me, the voices within the circles... They must be used for communication of some kind. I shudder to think what unnatural minds are contacted through such magic. Regardless, you seem to have emerged whole and sane. The Argent Dawn appreciates your service.
human-male

p:
You must've done something really bad to us or our friends, friend. At any rate, I'm here to offer you a way to get our good graces back.
As you know, Winterspring is quite cold. With so many of us goblins coming from other cities, we could use a hand keeping warm. Bring me some runecloth and coal and I'll put in the good word for ya. Be warned though, our enemies are not going to take kindly to your helping us.
c: Thank you, friend. You're on a quick path to redeeming yourself with our fair town.
goblin-male

d:
You'd better think twice before setting foot in Ratchet, friend! Words been getting around of your dirty deeds.
You're in luck though, a ship just arrived with many wounded from an encounter with the Bloodsail Buccaneers. This is your chance to prove you're not a complete scoundrel. Lend us a hand by bringing linen cloth for bandages and empty vials for potions.
goblin-female
p:
You'd better think twice before setting foot in Ratchet, friend! Word's been getting around of your dirty deeds.
You're in luck though, a ship just arrived with many wounded from an encounter with the Bloodsail Buccaneers. This is your chance to prove you're not a complete scoundrel. Lend us a hand by bringing linen cloth for bandages and empty vials for potions.
c: I'm happy you're seeing the error of your ways, friend. Keep the supplies coming; we're not going to forget about you so easily, friend!
goblin-female

p: You seek to befriend the goblins of Tanaris once again, friend? We're in need of materials for sails and guns to fight off our old enemies, the Bloodsail Buccaneers. Bring me mageweave and strong flux and we'll be on our way to pardoning your trespasses.
c: Keep it coming, friend. Us goblins don't forget that easily!
goblin-male

Yarrr... If ye be keen on enjoying the company of us experienced sea dogs, you'd best belay dressing like a blaggard! Here, put on something proper 'fore I keelhaul yer hide.
These'll fit ye better than they ever fit that old dog, Red-Eyed Ben. Lost him in a devil of a storm at sea.
Wear 'em with pride, mate!
human-male

d: On the corpse of the fallen abomination, you discover a cracked crystal, slowly pulsing with necrotic energy.
c:
Hm, you took this from the corpse of one of the invading abominations?
We have received word about the necropolis base camps that are being summoned by the Scourge. I suspect they wanted to create one inside Stormwind. It is good that they were unsuccessful.
human-male

d: You found this letter on one of the many Scourge minions you've slain. From its appearance and smell, it has been with the undead for some time. Perhaps someone at Light's Hope Chapel would be interested in examining it further...
p: Yes? What do you have there?
c:
How tragic. These words, clearly meant for someone the soldier loved, never made it to their destination. The events detailed happened years ago; I'm not sure if the intended recipient still lives.
There is hope yet, however. With the names and information he gives, I might be able to locate the family! It will take some research, but the librarian in Stormwind owes me a favor...
Thank you for bringing this to me. With your help, we may be able to grant someone peace of mind at last.
human-male
